text:
Coway’s latest air purifier earned a place among TIME’s best inventions of 2026, highlighting the Korean company’s efforts to make cleaner indoor air more accessible through improved filtration, quieter operation and automated monitoring.
The Airmega Mighty2 (AP-1512N) was selected in TIME’s household category, with the magazine describing it as “the double-duty air purifier” for combining air purification with real-time indoor air quality monitoring.
TIME evaluated nominations from its editors and correspondents worldwide, considering originality, effectiveness, ambition and impact, according to Coway’s announcement Monday.
The Mighty2 uses a three-stage filtration system featuring a high-efficiency particulate air filter that is 20 percent larger than its predecessor and an activated carbon filter that is 45 percent larger, designed to capture allergens, dust, pollen, mold, cooking fumes and wildfire smoke.
Its MegaScan laser sensor measures PM1, PM2.5 and PM10 particles, displaying numerical readings and using a four-color indicator to communicate air quality.
The purifier consumes 56 watts of power, which Coway says represents a 20 percent reduction in energy use, and operates at noise levels as low as 19 decibels.
The recognition builds on the reputation of its predecessor, the Airmega Mighty AP-1512HH, which Coway says was a longtime top pick at product review site Wirecutter and was inducted into its Hall of Fame in 2026.
The new model also received three major international design honors in 2026: the Red Dot Design Award, the iF Design Award and the International Design Excellence Awards.
A Coway official said the recognition affirmed the company’s commitment to combining filtration performance with user-focused design.
The Airmega Mighty2 is available in North America, with launches in Europe and Australia planned for the first quarter of 2027.
This article was published with the assistance of generative AI and edited by The Korea Times.
